newsitem.title: UK: More than 330 European economists savage EMU-paper.
newsitem.headline: More than 330 European economists savage EMU-paper.

text.p: More than 330 leading European economists have attacked the plan for a single European currency in an open letter to heads of government and are demanding that the rules be rewritten to foster jobs and growth.

The Guardian newspaper reported in its Thursday edition that 331 academics from 14 of the 15 European Union member states had signed the letter demanding that an EU summit this weekend in Amsterdam change the blueprint that entrenched deflationary policies.

The letter accused the EU's blueprint for economic and monetary union (EMU) of not helping the bloc's 20 million unemployed, its 50 million poor and of doing nothing to defend and extend the welfare state.

Given to newspapers across Europe and organised by three Dutch economists via the Internet computer network, the letter also said that EMU offered no perspective of an adequate response to environmental problems.

The Guardian quoted the letter as saying that while a common currency and monetary policy could have advantages, the tough rules for controlling government finances had "absolutely no economic basis" and could worsen recessions.
